title: 너의 그 잠깐이 전부야
sp: Korean Neo-Soul and contemporary R&B ballad with a laid-back, mid-tempo groove. The arrangement centers on a warm Rhodes electric piano playing jazzy extended chords with a slight tremolo and light chorus. The drum kit sits far behind the beat, with a soft, dry kick, a loose rimshot-style snare on the backbeat, brushed sixteenth-note closed hi-hats and occasional finger snaps. A thick, low-register electric bass follows a syncopated, rounded groove that locks with the kick. A clean electric guitar adds muted rhythmic accents and occasional melodic fills. Breathy male tenor vocals are delivered close to the microphone in an intimate, conversational tone, using a mix of chest voice, light falsetto and melismatic runs. Background vocals provide lush, multi-tracked harmonies and soft call-and-response adlibs. Production is warm and analog, with vinyl crackle, tape saturation and light room reverb on the vocals. Key of C Minor, 76 BPM, 4/4 time signature.

title: 그 소리는 창턱에서 기다렸다
sp: Korean cinematic post-rock in E minor at 76 BPM, built as one long unbroken crescendo. Opens nearly silent: a single clean electric guitar with heavy plate reverb, faint room tone, brushed snare, and a low sustained bass note holding under everything. Tremolo-picked electric guitars enter in slow layers, one after another, each washed in cavernous reverb and long delay tails so the space feels wider than the band. Restrained male vocals arrive late and low in the mix, half-buried in the reverb, closer to breath than to declaration, never belted. Drums grow from soft mallets to open toms to a full crashing kit. The final third is an explosive full-band swell: distorted guitar walls, cymbal swells, tremolo strings doubling the guitar line, bass distortion, everything ringing together. Then it thins out and disappears into room tone and tape hiss. Dynamics are the main instrument. Spacious, patient, aching, enormous at the end, silent at both edges.

title: 짧아서 따뜻한
sp: Bossa Nova. A nylon-string acoustic guitar plays syncopated bossa nova comping patterns with thumb-plucked bass notes and fingerstyle fills. An upright bass follows a traditional two-beat pattern focused on the root and fifth. Percussion consists of a drum kit played with brushes on the snare, a soft shaker, and a subtle rimshot accentuating the clave. A Rhodes piano provides sustained jazz-inflected chord extensions and occasional melodic fills. Soft, breathy female vocals are delivered in a low, close, whispered conversational style with minimal vibrato, sitting just above the guitar. The tempo is 96 BPM in 4/4 time, in A minor. The arrangement is sparse and unhurried, restrained in dynamics throughout, focusing on the interplay between the guitar's syncopation and the vocal's breath. The production is intimate with close-mic proximity on the vocal and guitar, set in a warm, short room reverb that keeps every sound near the listener.

title: 들릴 때만 산다
sp: Gospel and soul revival with a live congregational feel. A Hammond organ with a rotary speaker effect provides sustained chordal pads and occasional rhythmic stabs at the center of the arrangement. Electric bass plays warm, rounded lines with gospel passing tones. The drum kit uses a deep kick and a fat backbeat snare, with hand claps and tambourine on beats 2 and 4 growing denser through the song. Clean electric guitar adds short percussive chord stabs between vocal phrases. The lead vocalist delivers with soulful chest-voice power, melismatic runs, gritty rasp and frequent ad-libs, soul delivery, not operatic. A full choir answers every lead line in call-and-response, opening into massed unison and layered vocal harmonies at the peak. The arrangement builds in gradual layers, then settles into an extended vamp where the choir repeats one phrase over improvising organ. The tempo is 76 BPM in F major, 4/4 time. Live room production with natural reverb and warm analog compression.

title: 들릴 때만 나는 살아
sp: City Pop with elements of funk and synth-pop. Clean electric guitar plays syncopated muted strums and jazz-influenced chords with a bright chorus effect. A slap bass guitar performs busy sixteenth-note lines with frequent slides and pops. The drum kit features a gated reverb snare on 2 and 4, a tight kick, and sixteenth-note hi-hat patterns. Staccato analog synth brass stabs punctuate the transitions, while shimmering polyphonic pads and bell-like synth accents provide harmonic sheen. Smooth female vocals are delivered in a breathy, conversational alto with light doubling and layered harmonies in the chorus, brightening into head voice on the final refrain. A tenor saxophone melody enters during the instrumental break. The tempo is 116 BPM in D major, 4/4 time signature. Production features a polished, high-gloss nocturnal mix with wide stereo guitars, short plate reverb on the vocals, and warm analog tape sheen. The mood is buoyant and propulsive with a wistful, lingering afterglow.

title: 그 짧은 순간이 전 생애다
sp: Flamenco nuevo in D Phrygian, 128 BPM, driven by a hard twelve-count compas. A nylon-string flamenco guitar leads with violent rasgueado strumming, rapid picado runs across the low strings, and sharp golpe taps struck on the wooden body between chords. Hand claps, palmas, carry the rhythm in two layers: dry palmas sordas underneath and cracking open claps on the accents. A cajon plays deep bass tones with slapped high slaps on the offbeats. Heel stomps on a resonant wooden floor answer the guitar in call and response. Raw male vocals with long melismatic runs, guttural and ornamented, sliding between notes with cracked cries at the top of each phrase. The production is bone dry with almost no reverb, close-miked, so the fret noise, breath, and the wood of the instruments sit right in front of the listener. Dynamics swing violently: full ensemble attacks collapse into naked single-voice silence, then explode back with an abrupt unison stop before the last chord.

title: 기다리는 법만 배웠다
sp: Ambient drone piece in C major at 58 BPM. The arrangement is built on wide, sustained synthesizer pads that hold single chords for many bars, layered with a low-frequency sub-bass drone that lingers and slowly decays. There is almost no percussion; only an occasional soft mallet strike and a distant metallic shimmer mark the passing of time. Distant, breathy female vocalizations perform wordless melodic runs far back in the mix, heavily processed with a very long hall reverb tail so that each phrase blurs into the next. A high, glassy synth tone drifts in and out with slow filter swells. The stereo image is extremely wide and the dynamics move in long, patient crescendos and fades rather than sudden changes. The production emphasizes empty space, natural decay, and the sound of the room itself. The piece ends with the pads fading to silence.

title: 한 뼘의 시간
sp: A slow, wide-dynamic Korean ballad in B minor at 62 BPM, 4/4. It opens with a solo grand piano playing sparse pedaled chords, close-miked so the hammers and pedal release are audible. Soft male tenor vocals carry the verses with a breathy, intimate, restrained delivery, dry and centered. A string section enters quietly under the second verse, cellos and violas sustaining long legato lines beneath the piano. At the chorus the arrangement opens completely: the strings swell, soft kick and brushed snare arrive, and the vocal transitions into a powerful, belted chest voice at the top of the tenor range. Verses stay quiet and spare; every chorus is markedly louder and fuller than the one before. The bridge strips back to piano and one sustained cello, then rebuilds into the biggest final chorus with soaring violins and doubled belted vocals. The outro returns to solo grand piano, one note ringing into silence. Warm concert-hall production, wide dynamic range.

title: 발을 굴러 손을 쳐
sp: Afrobeat with highlife influence. A dense polyrhythmic percussion bed drives the whole arrangement: congas in interlocking offbeat patterns, a shaker holding a steady sixteenth-note pulse, talking drum answering with bent, speech-like phrases, and a cowbell on the downbeats. A clean electric guitar plays a short riff that repeats and cycles for the full track, with palm-muted scratches between phrases. The electric bass carries a thick, syncopated groove locked to a deep kick drum. A brass section of trumpet and saxophone delivers short stabs and sustained horn swells in call-and-response with the guitar. Group male vocals perform rhythmic chanting against a lead male tenor vocal in a call-and-response format, with a raw, shouted, energetic delivery. A tenor saxophone takes a brief improvised solo. Organ chords sustain underneath. 112 BPM in G minor, 4/4 time, cyclical and body-moving, with a long percussion breakdown before the final chorus.

sp: Celtic folk ballad in the Irish traditional style, in D major at 92 BPM in 6/8 time. The track opens with a solo tin whistle melody, unaccompanied and slightly breathy, before the ensemble gathers around it. A lead fiddle plays ornamented melodic lines with triplets, grace notes and double-stop accents, trading the theme with the whistle. A steel-string acoustic guitar provides steady rhythmic strumming with percussive palm mutes, while a mandolin adds eighth-note accompaniment and plays in unison with the fiddle in the refrains. A bodhran frame drum enters with a driving, syncopated pulse. Warm female vocals lead with a clear, airy delivery and gentle ornamentation, joined by layered vocal harmonies that swell in the choruses like a room of people singing together. The arrangement builds from sparse solo whistle to full ensemble and thins back out at the close. The production is warm, live and dry with minimal reverb, emphasizing the acoustic transients of plucked and bowed strings.
